terms.definition: The average mass of an element's atoms, measured in atomic mass units.
terms.function: Tells how heavy the element's atoms are on average, accounting for its isotope mixture.
terms.whereItIs: Printed below the atomic number on each element card of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: It connects atomic particles to measurable weight and is central to weighing out elements in chemistry.

terms.definition: The unit used to measure atomic mass; one amu is about the mass of a single proton or neutron.
terms.function: Gives chemists a scale small enough to weigh atoms, instead of everyday units like kilograms.
terms.whereItIs: The unit label attached to every atomic mass value.
terms.whyItMatters: Without amu, atomic masses would be awkwardly tiny numbers in kilograms.

terms.definition: The positive particle in the nucleus, weighing about 1 amu.
terms.function: Contributes roughly half of an atom's mass and defines the element.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the nucleus cluster, shown as the coral spheres.
terms.whyItMatters: Proton and neutron counts together set an atom's mass number.

terms.definition: The neutral particle in the nucleus, weighing about 1 amu.
terms.function: Adds mass without changing the element; its count varies between isotopes.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the nucleus cluster, shown as the graphite spheres.
terms.whyItMatters: Neutron differences between isotopes are what make atomic masses averages instead of single numbers.
